title: NovaQuill - time to first API token & hosting path discovery
next_steps: Send quickstart link and free credits instructions
Share SOC2 + VM/VPC security pack link
Schedule 1hr technical deep dive (SE-led) for next week
Spin up pilot project and provide estimated cost for 100k tokens/day
action_items: Alex - Email quickstart guide + credit redemption steps by 2026-06-26
Priya - Prepare simple perf matrix for hosted vs dedicated within 3 days
Ravi - Confirm internal budget and timeline for pilot by 2026-07-02
summary: Intro call to understand NovaQuill's requirements for an LLM inference provider. Customer is evaluating Redwood's hosted API for fast time-to-first-token via PLG credits, with potential move to Dedicated/Private for HIPAA-like data regs. Key concerns: latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/KMS options, SOC2 evidence, and migration path to Dedicated. Agreed next steps: share quickstart + credits, security docs, schedule SE-led deep dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya our Solutions Engineer is here too. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Jordan: Jordan Lee here, CTO at NovaQuill, Mei and Ravi also on.
[00:17] Mei: Mei Chen, product lead. Hi all.
[00:20] Alex: Awesome. We're penciled for 40 minutes, we'll keep it tight. High level goal — understand your latency/cost targets, data concerns, and get you to first token quickly via our PLG path.
[00:32] Priya: Hi, Priya, thanks. I can follow up with technical detail, perf numbers, and a plan for a pilot.
[00:38] Jordan: Sounds good. Our main ask: get started fast, ideally self-serve credits so product team can experiment. But infra has strict controls — we might need a private/VPC plan for certain workflows.
[00:49] Alex: Perfect, that's a common path — start on Hosted with credits for time-to-first-token, then Dedicated or Private for regulated data. Quick question: what's your expected concurrency and tokens/day for the experiment?
[01:02] Mei: For the first experiment, maybe 10k to 20k tokens/day, low concurrency — mostly interactive UI tests. If it proves out, we could bump to 100k tokens/day within a quarter.
[01:12] Ravi: From infra side, the long term ask is predictable latency under 200ms for short prompts and throughput for batch jobs. Also we need to confirm KMS integration and audit logs.
[01:23] Sasha: Security — we need SOC2 evidence, SAML SSO, and control over retention. Anything containing PII will have to run in a private deployment.
[01:32] Alex: All fair. To outline options quickly: Hosted (PLG) — fastest to get going, we can issue trial credits and you can call the Redwood API in minutes. Dedicated — reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput; Private — VPC or on-prem for regulatory constraints with customer-managed KMS.
[01:46] Jordan: On Hosted, do you have templates or starter prompts for product teams? We want low friction for non-engineers.
[01:53] Priya: Yes — quickstart repo and SDK examples (JS/Python). We'll share a one-click Postman collection and an example react widget for tokenization and streaming. The quickstart usually gets teams to first token in under 15 minutes if credentials are ready.
[02:07] Mei: That'd be great. Do you provide free credits? How many?
[02:10] Alex: We typically extend PLG credits — for product trials we'll give a set amount (we'll confirm exact amount in the follow-up email). It covers basic experiments; for heavier POCs we can bump credits or set up a short reserved pilot.
[02:21] Ravi: If we start on Hosted but need VPC later, how seamless is the migration?
[02:25] Priya: You can pin model versions and configs. The API surface is the same across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Migration requires a bit of ops — exporting any cached KV prefixes isn't necessary because we rely on model deterministic outputs; however for very latency-sensitive apps we'd recommend a Dedicated cluster with burst capacity. We'll document step-by-step.
[02:44] Jordan: Can you talk about latency tradeoffs? We're worried about cost if we have to overprovision.
[02:49] Priya: Sure. Hosted uses multi-tenant pools and autoscaling; latency averages depend on chosen model, quantization, and batching window. You can choose lower-cost quantized variants for most tasks. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and predictable p95 latency; cost is higher but unit price per token can drop if volume is steady. We can model a 100k tokens/day workload and show cost/latency curves.
[03:12] Sasha: KMS — can Redwood integrate with our customer-managed KMS for key wrapping?
[03:16] Alex: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer KMS integrations and envelope encryption options; for Hosted we have trusted key management but can provide attestations. We'll include the security pack link.
[03:28] Mei: About data retention — will logs or prompts be stored? We need to make sure anything PII is not kept.
[03:34] Priya: We have retention controls; by default Hosted will retain logs for troubleshooting, but you can opt out or configure redaction. Private deployments leave logs under your control. We'll share the retention options doc.
[03:46] Jordan: What's the friction to onboard product folks without infra? Can they sign up and get tokens without engineering involvement?
[03:52] Alex: Yes, self-serve signup gives API tokens via the console. The quickest path: sign up, claim PLG credits, copy token, call the endpoint. We also provide client SDKs and UI widgets.
[04:03] Mei: That is ideal. Could you also provide sandbox projects for multiple teams?
[04:06] Priya: We support organizations and projects; each project can have separate tokens and RBAC. We'll outline that in the guide.
[04:15] Ravi: Any constraints on model sizes or sequence lengths in Hosted?
[04:19] Priya: Hosted supports curated open models and we publish profiles per model (latency/cost/seq-length). Very long sequences will increase cost; we can recommend truncation and KV caching for chat-like apps to mitigate.
[04:32] Jordan: About benchmarks — do you have public perf numbers or will you run a custom bench for us?
[04:36] Alex: We have published profiles but for a reliable comparison we'll run a short benchmark tailored to your prompt set. Priya can run a small perf job or provide a spreadsheet template to feed your prompts.
[04:48] Priya: For the benchmark I'd need a sample of 50-100 representative prompts and desired SLOs. I'll prepare an execution plan and expected metrics (p50, p95 latency, tokens/sec).
[04:58] Mei: We'll push a prompt set after the call.
[05:01] Sasha: Regarding compliance, will you share SOC2 Type II and penetration test results?
[05:06] Alex: Yes, we can share SOC2 summary and our pen test attestation under an NDA or via our security portal link. We'll include the security deck in the follow-up.
[05:18] Jordan: On pricing transparency — we need a predictable per-token estimate for budgeting.
[05:23] Alex: We'll provide a cost estimate matrix: hosted per-token retail, dedicated reserved pricing, and estimated savings at scale. We'll also show how batching and caching affect unit cost.
[05:35] Ravi: Can Redwood do SAML or SCIM for org provisioning?
[05:39] Priya: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for enterprise plans; we'll include setup docs.
[05:46] Mei: Any gotchas for front-end streaming responses? We want partial tokens to render as they arrive.
[05:52] Priya: We support streaming across SDKs and have examples for browser-safe streaming. There can be cross-origin caveats but we have proxy patterns.
[06:02] Jordan: For PII-sensitive workloads — will we need Private from day one?
[06:06] Sasha: Our security policy says production PII must be in customer-controlled VPC. So pilot can be non-PII on Hosted, but anything regulated moves to Private.
[06:15] Alex: Totally reasonable. Many customers run feature flagged workflows: public features on Hosted, regulated ones on Private.
[06:22] Mei: What's typical time to stand up Dedicated vs Private?
[06:25] Priya: Dedicated — a few days to a couple weeks depending on capacity and contract. Private/VPC — usually 2-6 weeks for VPC peering, KMS setup, and audit steps. On-prem longer.
[06:38] Jordan: Can you summarize a recommended path for us?
[06:41] Alex: Suggested path: 1) Start Hosted with PLG credits and quickstart to get product teams to first token within hours. 2) Run an SE-led benchmark and pilot for target workload (Priya runs). 3) If PII/regulatory constraints are required, plan Dedicated first then transition to Private with a targeted timeline and SSO/KMS config.
[06:59] Mei: That aligns with our plan.
[07:02] Ravi: Can you also include a rough cost forecast for 100k tokens/day for both hosted and dedicated?
[07:08] Alex: We'll include an example cost sheet. Priya, can you model a 100k/day scenario?
[07:12] Priya: Yep — I can produce a simple spreadsheet showing hosted retail and dedicated reserved pricing and estimated savings with batching.
[07:20] Jordan: Any notes on SLA and support during a pilot?
[07:24] Samir: Samir here from CSM — for pilots we provide onboarding support, weekly syncs, and a war-room for issues. SLA applies for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has standard uptime terms and we can discuss enhanced SLAs for enterprise arrangements.
[07:36] Mei: Great. Can we get a checklist of artifacts you'll send?
[07:39] Alex: We'll send: quickstart guide + SDK links, credit redemption steps, security pack (SOC2 + pen test summary), SSO/SCIM docs, a perf template sheet, and a proposed pilot scope doc. Links will be in the follow-up email.
[07:54] Jordan: Perfect. Any concerns about vendor lock-in if we later move between deployment modes?
[07:59] Priya: Our API is consistent; models and configs are portable. There is some ops work as you move infra, but we avoid proprietary formats. We can outline a migration checklist.
[08:11] Mei: If we want to do a short POC to wave off latency concerns, how quickly can you run a dedicated perf test with our prompts?
[08:18] Priya: If you share prompts within 48 hours, I can run a small job and deliver p50/p95 numbers within 72 hours. Depends on queue but we prioritize pilot customers.
[08:29] Jordan: We'll send a set today.
[08:32] Sasha: A couple of small questions — are logs encrypted at rest and do you provide fine-grained RBAC?
[08:40] Alex: Yes, logs encrypted at rest; RBAC with project-level roles is supported. We'll include the RBAC mapping doc.
[08:49] Mei: Any pitfalls you've seen with teams trying to self-serve?
[08:53] Priya: Most friction points: missing CORS or streaming config in front end, not using token rotation best practices, and underestimating prompt costs. Our quickstart covers these.
[09:05] Alex: Quick administrative — I'll drop links and the credit redemption instructions. Priya will own the perf deliverable. Samir will coordinate pilot support and weekly check-ins. Ravi will confirm budget.
[09:18] Jordan: Sounds good.
[09:20] Mei: Thanks.
[09:22] Alex: Any other open questions?
[09:24] Ravi: One more — for Dedicated, do you support bring-your-own-cloud (BYOC) or is it hosted by Redwood?
[09:29] Priya: We offer both: Redwood-managed Dedicated in our regions, or dedicated clusters in your cloud account with peering for BYOC in certain deployments. We'll specify options in the follow-up.
[09:40] Jordan: That's useful.
[09:43] Alex: Ok we'll recap. Next steps: Alex send quickstart + credits + security pack; Priya run perf bench once you send prompts; Samir schedule weekly pilot sync; NovaQuill to confirm pilot timeline and budget. Any dates?
[09:58] Mei: We aim to start the pilot by 2026-07-06.
[10:03] Alex: Noted. We'll target the SE deep dive for week of 2026-06-29. I'll ping a few times to lock in.
[10:10] Jordan: Thanks, appreciate it.
[10:13] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the email and links.
[10:18] Mei: Bye.
[10:19] Priya: Bye.
[10:20] [call ends]
